textbookText: Augustin-Louis Cauchy was a French mathematician and physicist. He was born on August 21, 1789 in Paris, France, and died on May 23, 1857 in Sceaux. Cauchy was one of the greatest of modern mathematicians. In mathematics, Cauchy pioneered in analysis and the theory of substitution groups. In optics, Cauchy defined an empirical relationship between the refractive index and the wavelength of light for a particular transparent material in 1837. This relation is called Cauchy's transmission equation. In 1816, Cauchy won the grand prix of the Institute of France for a paper on wave propagation which is now accepted as a classic in hydrodynamics. In 1822 he laid the foundations of the mathematical theory of elasticity. Cauchy made substantial contributions to the theory of numbers and wrote three important papers on error theory. His work on optics provided a mathematical basis for the workable but somewhat unsatisfactory theory of the properties of the ether, a hypothetical, omnipresent medium once thought to be the conductor of light. His collected works, Oeuvres complètesd’Augustin Cauchy (1882–1970), were published in 27 volumes.

deviation? 16.1 Introduction A prism is a seemingly simple but versatile optical tool. Study of prism provides a gateway to a world of optical phenomena and applications of light. A prism is a simple triangular slab of glass but it has a pivotal role in taking out the mysteries of dispersion of light, spectrum of the rainbow, fundamental properties of light itself and many more. A prism has applications from spectroscopy and photography to telecommunications and beyond. In this chapter we study about the refraction of light through prism in detail.

A homogenous transparent refracting medium enclosed by two plane surfaces meeting each other along a straight edge as shown in figure 16.1 is called a prism. The angle between the refracting surfaces is called the refracting angle or angle of prism. The section cut by a plane (XYZ) perpendicular to the refracting surfaces is called the principal section of the prism.

Consider an equilateral glass prism XYZ having angle of prism A. When a ray of light strikes the of face XY at a point Q, it suffers refraction along QR. Refracted ray QR also strikes on the next refracting face XZ and again undergoes refraction. Finally, the ray of light emerges out along RS as shown in figure 16.2.
